chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man is found to have been killed, if a complete limb is found for him, he is prayed upon and buried; and if a complete limb is not found for him, he is not prayed upon and is buried.

key_terms.صُلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ: he was prayed upon (funeral prayer performed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on funeral prayer for a killed person whose body is incomplete?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the juristic criteria for performing Salat al-Janazah on a murder victim whose body is incomplete, establishing that the presence of a 'complete limb' (such as a hand, foot, or head) necessitates the full funeral prayer, while its absence exempts the deceased. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on physical integrity as a sign of dignity and completeness for ritual honors, distinguishing such cases from those of martyrs or those with specific exemptions. The criterion ensures that the deceased is treated with the respect due to a whole person, even if the majority of the body is missing.
